english: From the point $P(2,4)$, two tangents are drawn to the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{21}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{15}=1$. These tangents meet the $x$-axis at the points $A$ and $B$. Then the area of the triangle $PAB$ is ______.
hindi: बिन्दु $P(2,4)$ से दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{21}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{15}=1$ पर दो स्पर्श रेखाएँ खींची जाती हैं। ये स्पर्श रेखाएँ $x$-अक्ष को बिन्दुओं $A$ तथा $B$ पर मिलती हैं। तब त्रिभुज $PAB$ का क्षेत्रफल ______ है।
solution_full: $P(2,4)$ is outside the ellipse since $\dfrac{4}{21}+\dfrac{16}{15}-1=\dfrac{20+112-105}{105}>0$, so two tangents exist. Neither is vertical, because $x=2$ is not a tangent ($2^{2}\ne21$).
A line of slope $m$ through $P$ is $y=mx+(4-2m)$; it touches the ellipse iff $(4-2m)^{2}=21m^{2}+15$, i.e. $16-16m+4m^{2}=21m^{2}+15$, so $17m^{2}+16m-1=0$.
Tangent with slope $\dfrac1{17}$: $y=\dfrac{x+66}{17}$, meeting the $x$-axis at $A(-66,0)$. Tangent with slope $-1$: $y=6-x$, meeting the $x$-axis at $B(6,0)$.
$AB=72$ and the height of $P$ above the $x$-axis is $4$, so the area of $\triangle PAB$ is $\dfrac12\cdot72\cdot4=144$.
originality_note: New: the triangle cut off on the x-axis by the two tangents from a point, where one tangent is almost horizontal and gives a far intercept (way 5). Closest known: area of the triangle formed by the two tangents and the chord of contact. Different because: the base is on the x-axis, so the slopes themselves (from the tangency condition) are needed, not the chord-of-contact formula. Standard ingredient.
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, point and curve introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked that P is outside, that no tangent is vertical or horizontal (both meet the x-axis), and that the slopes are rational so the area is exact. Changed: No change.
key_step: Tangency condition through P gives 17m^2 + 16m - 1 = 0, slopes 1/17 and -1.
justification: Routine chain: tangency condition, quadratic in m, intercepts, area. Comparable to 2024-P1-Q4 (L2), tangents from an external point to an ellipse.
blueprint_concepts: tangents drawn from an external point to a Ellipse

concept_use.tangents drawn from an external point to: The two tangents from the external point P(2,4) are found from (4 - 2m)^2 = 21m^2 + 15, giving slopes 1/17 and -1 and the x-intercepts -66 and 6.
